- Solvent: triethylene glycol + ethanol (EtOH).  
- Process: microwave solvothermal treatment at 180 °C, 300 W, 2.45 GHz, 60 min in a TANK eco-microwave reactor.

- Low-fluorine MOD route (reference [21] cited; exact fluorine content not given).

- Substrate: industrial 5-layer tape LaMnO₃/MgO/Y₂O₃/Al₂O₃/Hastelloy.  
- Seed layer: 200–300 nm pure YBCO precursor first coated to act as self-seeding layer.  
- Main layer: three successive coats of BHO-doped YBCO precursor; total YBCO thickness 2.4 µm.  
- Each coat pyrolysed ≈ 20 min (temperature not specified).

Reconstructed from multiple sections of the PDF:  
- Multistep growth: one-third of conventional growth at 785 °C → direct cooling → re-heating through full conventional profile; total high-temperature dwell ≈ 40 min.

- TEM: JEOL JEM-2100 F field-emission HRTEM for BHO size distributions; cross-sections prepared by FEI Helios Nanolab 600i FIB.  
- STEM: high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) imaging and geometric phase analysis (GPA) for local strain mapping.  
- XRD: powder patterns of as-synthesised BHO (instrument not specified).

- Transport Ic: 1-m-long tapes tested with EASTFORCE M-Corder at 77 K, self-field; selected samples also measured at 30 K and under applied field (angle-dependent data collected).  
- Pinning force density Fp derived from magnetisation Jc(B).

- Size statistics from TEM images (>100 particles).  
- Coarsening factor = final BHO size / pristine BHO size.  
- Particle density estimated assuming random uniform distribution.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1 – Substrate preparation  
Start from commercial buffered metallic tapes: Hastelloy C-276 / Al₂O₃ / Y₂O₃ / IBAD-MgO / LaMnO₃. (No further substrate fabrication details are given.)

Step 2 – Target preparation (not experimentally detailed)  
Prepare two separate ceramic targets:  
- EuBCO + 2–5 mol % BaHfO₃ (for nano-rods)  
- YBCO + 5–25 mol % excess Y (for Y₂O₃ nano-particles)  
Exact dopant concentrations are proprietary and not disclosed.

Step 3 – Pulsed-laser deposition (PLD) of REBCO layers  
Deposit REBCO layers at Faraday Factory Japan LLC using a Coherent LEAP-300C laser (300 Hz, 900–1000 mJ pulse energy).  
- Eu-NR sample: single EuBCO layer, tEu-NR = 1.58 µm.  
- Y-NP sample: single YBCO layer, tY-NP = 1.85 µm.  
- Eu-NR/Y-NP bilayer: first deposit 1.65 µm EuBCO (Eu-NR), then deposit 1.45 µm YBCO (Y-NP) without breaking vacuum, giving total REBCO thickness 3.1 µm.  
Substrate temperature, oxygen pressure, and growth rate are not specified.

Step 4 – Ag protection layer  
Immediately after REBCO growth, cover the film with 2 µm Ag by magnetron sputtering at room temperature.

Step 5 – Oxygenation anneal  
Anneal the finished tapes at 300–400 °C for 12 h in flowing O₂ to optimize carrier concentration. Heating/cooling profiles are not provided.

Step 6 – Micro-bridge patterning  
Cut 4-mm-wide tapes into pieces. Use a 10-ps pulsed laser to ablate a 1-mm-long, ≈50-µm-wide micro-bridge (exact widths: 46.0 µm for Y-NP, 51.4 µm for Eu-NR and bilayer) through the Ag and REBCO layers, reducing the critical current below 20 A.

Step 7 – Critical current density Jc(T,B,θ) measurement  
Mount the bridge on a rotatable sample stage in a gas-He-flow cryostat (Janis Research) equipped with a 15-T cryogen-free magnet (JASTEC).  
- Temperature set-points: 65, 69, 73, 77.3, 81 K (Cernox thermometer beside sample).  
- Magnetic field: 0–15 T, applied direction θ varied from −30° to +120° (θ = 0° ↔ B ‖ c-axis; θ = 90° ↔ B ‖ ab-plane) by stepper motor; angle monitored by motor pulses and a Hall sensor (HG-166A-2U).  
- Transport current limit: 20 A DC; current always perpendicular to B (J ⊥ B).  
- Record V–I curves with standard four-probe technique.  
- Define Jc at each (T,B,θ) by fitting V(I) to E(J) = Ec(J/Jc)^n with Ec = 1 µV cm⁻¹.

Step 8 – Pinning force analysis  
Convert Jc(T,B) to volume pinning force density Fp = Jc·B for B ‖ c. Fit Fp(B) curves to the Dew-Hughes-type expression to extract exponents p, q, peak field Bpeak, and irreversibility field Birr (criterion: Jc = 10 A cm⁻²).

Step 9 – Microstructure characterisation  
Take a 17 µm × 15 µm cross-section from the same bilayer tape by FIB (Versa 3D & Quanta 3D). Image in STEM (JEOL JEM-ARM200F, 200 kV) in high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) mode. Acquire spatially resolved EDS maps (Y-L, Eu-L, Ba-L, Cu-K, Hf-M) to verify layer separation and identify Y₂O₃ nano-particles (10–30 nm) and BaHfO₃ nano-rods (≈40 nm long, tilted).

[Experimental Design Details]
- Sample set: three conductors—Y-NP, Eu-NR, Eu-NR/Y-NP—differing only in REBCO layer composition and stacking.  
- Total REBCO thicknesses: 1.85 µm (Y-NP), 1.58 µm (Eu-NR), 3.1 µm (bilayer).  
- Bridge geometry normalises electric-field criterion to 1 µV cm⁻¹; current capacity kept ≤20 A to avoid heating.  
- Angular scan resolution and step size are not specified.  
- Lorentz force density |Fem| ≲50 GN m⁻³ at T≥77.3 K, B>0, θ>90°—authors state this is low enough to avoid delamination in their set-up.  
- No details on sample mounting glue, wire bonding, or voltage tap separation.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Substrate provision  
- Use commercial IBAD-MgO metal substrates (source: Dr. Izumi & Dr. Ibi, AIST; no further substrate details given).

Step 2: Three-layer VLS growth (all layers in same PLD chamber, KrF excimer laser λ = 248 nm)  
  a) “Solid” layer – deposit 200 nm YBCO at 860 °C, 53 Pa O₂, 100 Hz laser, YBCO target.  
  b) “Liquid” layer – deposit 50 nm Ba-Cu-O (+10 wt % Ag₂O) at 860 °C, 200 Pa O₂, 10 Hz laser, Ba₃Cu₇O₁₀+Ag₂O target.  
  c) “Vapor” layer – deposit YBCO at 940 °C, 200 Pa O₂, 100 Hz laser, YBCO target; vary deposition time to obtain final thickness 0.74–3.5 µm (total film 0.94–3.7 µm).

Step 3: Post-growth oxygen anneal  
- Cut 2 × 2 mm² pieces with UV-laser marker; anneal 400 °C, 2 h, flowing O₂.

Step 4: Structural & compositional characterisation  
- XRD 2θ-ω → obtain (200)/(006) intensity ratio → a-axis grain fraction.  
- Rocking curve on (005) reflection → Δω (FWHM).  
- ϕ-scan on (103) → Δϕ (FWHM).  
- SEM + EDX → surface precipitates, morphology.  
- ICP-OES → film composition & thickness.

Step 5: Transport Tc measurement  
- Four-probe resistivity vs temperature → Tc (90.0 K, 90.8 K, 90.6 K for 0.94, 1.4, 3.7 µm films respectively).

Step 6: Magnetisation relaxation (SQUID MPMS)  
- Field parallel to c-axis; temperature 30–77 K.  
- Protocol: apply high field → reduce to set value → record magnetic moment m(t) for 10²–10³ s.  
- Convert m(t) to J(t) and E(t) via eqs. (1)–(2) using sample dimensions l, w, d and geometry factor G (values of G not given).  
- Fit ln(m/m₀) vs ln t → slope = –kBT/U*₀ → extract U*₀; m₀ obtained by extrapolating relaxation curve to t = 1 s.

Step 7: Data analysis  
- Plot Jc(B,T) and U*₀(B,T) for three thicknesses.  
- Additional creep-flow model analysis (parameters in Table 3) performed only for 0.94 µm film; theoretical Jc(B) curves for 3.7 µm obtained by scaling thickness d while keeping other pinning parameters fixed.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Three final thicknesses studied: 0.94 µm, 1.4 µm, 3.7 µm.  
- All samples show Tc > 90 K and low a-axis grain ratio (≤ 2.8 %).  
- Δω (005) FWHM: 0.72°, 0.63°, 0.70°; Δϕ (103) FWHM: 1.48°, 1.49°, 1.35° respectively (3.7 µm film shows extra 45°-offset peak).  
- Surface precipitates (Cu-rich, Y-poor “droplets”) seen on 0.94 & 1.4 µm films; 3.7 µm film rougher, fewer droplets.  
- Magnetisation relaxation measured at fixed fields up to 5 T (exact field list not specified).  
- Electric-field criterion for Jc: Ec = 1 × 10⁻⁸ V m⁻¹ (stated only in modelling section).

Step 7: Microstructure imaging – Acquire cross-sectional and plan-view TEM images (JEOL JEM-2100 F) to visualize nanorod morphology, measure nanorod dimensions/spacing, and statistically evaluate number density (>600 nanorods counted per sample).

- Statistics: nanorod density/width obtained by counting >600 rods across multiple plan-view TEM images for 15 and 25 mol% samples.

- Place stoichiometric CeO₂ (99.9 %, Crytur) in a beaker, add 1:1 (vol.) diluted HNO₃ (stoichiometric ratio CeO₂:HNO₃ = 1:4.5) and heat the suspension to 80 °C.  
- Add 30 % H₂O₂ (LachNer) drop-wise under continued heating until the solid CeO₂ fully dissolves, forming Ce(III) nitrate solution.

Step 2 – Dissolution of Ba(OH)₂·8H₂O  
- In a separate beaker suspend Ba(OH)₂·8H₂O (p.a., FLUKA) in water.  
- Add concentrated HNO₃ drop-wise until the hydroxide completely dissolves.

Step 3 – Solution mixing and concentration adjustment  
- Combine the two clear solutions and dilute with water to obtain a total cation concentration of 0.1 mol L⁻¹.

Step 4 – Reverse co-precipitation  
- Prepare an aqueous receiver solution containing NH₃ and H₂O₂ (exact concentrations not specified).  
- Add the 0.1 mol L⁻¹ Ba/Ce nitrate solution drop-wise into the NH₃/H₂O₂ receiver under stirring (no further details on addition rate or temperature given).

Step 5 – Precipitate work-up  
- Wash the resulting solid with concentrated aqueous NH₃ (concentration not quantified).  
- Filter, then dry the powder at 110 °C for 12 h.

Step 6 – Heat treatment / crystallisation  
- Place dried powder in a furnace, heat at 10 °C min⁻¹ to either 800 °C or 1000 °C, hold 60 min, then cool rapidly to room temperature.

Step 7 – Characterisation sequence  
- Record simultaneous DTA/TG/MS (heating rate 10 K min⁻¹, flowing air) on the 110 °C-dried precursor.  
- Collect X-ray diffraction (Co Kα, Bruker AXS D2 Phaser, Bragg-Brentano geometry) on as-dried and on annealed powders; analyse phases with HighScore Plus and PDF-4 database; perform Rietveld refinement and Williamson–Hall line-broadening analysis to extract crystallite sizes.  
- Acquire Raman spectra (DXR Microscope, Thermo Scientific; Nd:YAG laser, multichannel CCD) over 0.01–1000 µm range; inspect CeO₂ T₂g band (≈465 cm⁻¹), BaCeO₃ lattice modes (50–400 cm⁻¹) and BaCO₃ symmetric stretch (≈1060 cm⁻¹).  
- Image powder morphology with SEM (Lyra3 GMU FIB-SEM, Tescan).

- Precipitation chemistry: avoids carbonate/oxalate precipitants; relies on pH-driven re-oxidation of Ce(III)→CeO₂ and low solubility of Ba(OH)₂ at high pH.  
- Target phases: BaCeO₃ (major) and CeO₂ (inevitable secondary phase because Ba precipitation is incomplete).  
- Annealing temperatures chosen on the basis of DTA/TG CO₂-release feature observed at ≈850 °C.  
- Grain-size evaluation performed only for the two main phases (BaCeO₃ and CeO₂) using the same Williamson–Hall formalism.  
- No further processing (e.g., grinding, sieving, pelletising) is mentioned after heat treatment.

Step 1 – Precursor powder synthesis  
- Sm-211, Eu-211 and Gd-211 powders: stoichiometric mixtures of Sm₂O₃/Eu₂O₃/Gd₂O₃ (Kojundo) + BaO₂ + CuO were calcined 12 h each at 860 °C, 900 °C, 950 °C with intermediate grindings.  
- SEG-211 precursor: equal-weight mixture of the three 211 powders + 0.5 wt % Pt.  
- Liquid-source powder: 1:1 weight mixture of Y-123 (Y₂O₃ + BaO₂ + CuO calcined 860–920 °C) and Ba₃Cu₅O₈ (BaO₂ + CuO calcined 860 & 880 °C).  

Step 2 – BaO₂ doping series  
- Batches of SEG-211 were admixed with 0–5 wt % BaO₂ (samples Ba-0 to Ba-5).  

Step 3 – Pellet assembly (TSIG stack)  
- 20-mm-diameter pellets: SEG-211 (top) / liquid-source (bottom) at weight ratio 1.3 : 1.  
- A c-axis-oriented NdBa₂Cu₃Oᵧ seed crystal was placed on top of the SEG-211 pellet.  
- Whole stack was supported underneath by Y₂O₃ powder layer + MgO crystal to limit liquid loss.  

Step 4 – Single-domain growth heat treatment (air atmosphere)  
- Heat to 1080 °C at 100 °C h⁻¹, hold 1 h.  
- Slow cool 1060 → 1020 °C over ≈150 h, then furnace cool to room temperature.  

Step 5 – Oxygenation  
- Anneal 450 → 350 °C for 250 h in flowing O₂ (250 ml min⁻¹).  

Step 6 – Ag₂O-added sample (SEG-Ag)  
- Identical precursor preparation but with 4 wt % BaO₂ + 10 wt % Ag₂O in SEG-211.  
- Because Ag₂O lowers peritectic T by ~25 °C, both maximum and slow-cooling temperatures were reduced by 25 °C; other parameters (ramp rate, dwell, oxygenation) unchanged.  

Step 7 – Structural verification  
- X-ray diffraction on 2 × 2 mm ab-plane cleavage pieces (Cu-Kα); (00l) peaks used to confirm single-domain character and to extract c-lattice parameter.  

Step 8 – Superconducting property measurements  
- Tc and ΔTc: zero-field-cooled (ZFC) DC magnetic susceptibility at 1 mT (H // c) using SQUID; pieces cut ~2 mm below seed.  
- Jc(H,T): magnetisation hysteresis (M–H) loops up to 5 T at 80, 77, 75, 65 K (H // c) on ~1.5 × 1.5 × 0.5 mm³ specimens; Jc extracted via extended Bean model (Eq. 1).  

Step 9 – Microstructural analysis  
- Field-emission SEM (JEOL-7100F, 1500×) on ab-plane ~2 mm below surface; 211 particle size distribution evaluated with ImageJ.  

Step 10 – Flux-pinning analysis  
- Volume pinning force Fp = B·Jc(77 K); irreversibility field Hirr taken at Jc = 100 A cm⁻²; normalised curves Fp/Fp,max vs h = H/Hirr fitted to Fp/Fp,max = A h^p (1–h)^q to extract hmax = p/(p+q) and identify pinning regime.  

[Experimental Design Details]
- All processing performed in ambient air (no controlled pO₂).  
- Liquid-source / 211 weight ratio fixed at 1.3 for every sample.  
- Pt (0.5 wt %) added to refine 211 particles; no other dopants except specified BaO₂ and Ag₂O.

- Starting oxides: Y₂O₃, BaCO₃, CuO.  
- Three stoichiometric mixtures prepared:  
  – Y123 (YBa₂Cu₃O₇−δ)  
  – Y211 (Y₂BaCuO₅)  
  – Y023 (Ba₂Cu₃Oₓ)  
- Each mixture calcined twice (40 h per calcination) at 930 °C (Y123), 950 °C (Y211) and 880 °C (Y023).

Step 2 – Precursor powder blending  
- CPP: 35 mol % Y211 + balance Y123 + 1 wt % CeO₂.  
- MPP: 72.34 mol % Y₂O₃ (Y200) + Y023 + 1 wt % CeO₂.  
- Blending performed by ball-milling; no further milling parameters given.

Step 3 – Green-body preparation  
- 40 g powder pressed into 30 mm × 30 mm square pellets (thickness not specified).  
- C-MPP pellet: 20 g CPP powder placed above 20 g MPP powder in the same die and co-pressed.  
- Identical uniaxial pressing conditions used for all pellets (pressure value not specified).

Step 4 – Seed/buffer/substrate assembly (same for all pellets)  
- Top surface: one polished SmBCO single-crystal seed (a–b plane down).  
- Buffer mini-pellet (6 mm Ø × 2 mm thick, made from CPP) inserted between seed and main pellet.  
- Bottom layer: substrate of Y123 + Yb₂O₃ powders (functions as extra liquid source and nucleation barrier).  
- Entire assembly placed in furnace as illustrated in Fig. 1.

Step 5 – Top-seeded melt-growth (TSMG) heat treatment (all samples processed together)  
- Ramp to T_max = 1050 °C in 12 h; dwell 1.5 h.  
- Cool to T_s = 1010 °C at 80 °C h⁻¹ to initiate epitaxial growth.  
- Undercooling: 120 h linear cool to T_e = 970 °C.  
- Furnace cool to room temperature.  
- Seed, buffer and substrate mechanically removed afterwards.

Step 6 – Oxygenation  
- Samples annealed at 450 °C in flowing O₂ for 220 h.

Step 7 – Dimensional inspection and cutting  
- Samples measured (callipers) to obtain a–b plane area and c-axis thickness (Table 2).  
- Each bulk cut along the c-axis through the centre with a precision diamond wire saw.  
- Cut surface ground and polished with a precision diamond surface grinder/polisher.

Step 8 – Optical microstructure characterisation  
- Polished a–c cross-sections imaged with an optical microscope.  
- Three to four local regions (positions 1–3/4) selected for porosity quantification.  
- ImageJ software used to count pores (n) and measure average pore diameter (D).  
- Porosity calculated as (n × D)/S, where S is the inspected area (~2.71 mm²).

Step 9 – Levitation-force measurement  
- Instrument: custom-built SCML-05 platform (Fig. 3).  
- Magnet: second track of a Halbach NdFeB guideway; surface field 0.67 T at working height (WH) 5 mm.  
- Temperature: 77 K by continuous liquid-nitrogen cooling.  
- Two magnetisation modes:  
  – Zero-field cooling (ZFC): sample cooled at 60 mm above track, then lowered to 5 mm.  
  – Field cooling (FC): sample cooled at 30 mm above track, then lowered to 5 mm.  
- Procedure (identical for ZFC and FC):  
  1. Cool to 77 K at fixed height (ZFCH or FCH).  
  2. Lower to WH = 5 mm and immediately retract at 1 mm s⁻¹ to record force loop.  
  3. Lower again at 1 mm s⁻¹, hold 3 min to record force-relaxation curve.  
- Force data sampled continuously; maximum force (F_max) and minimum force after 3 min (F_min) extracted.  
- Relaxation rate R = (F_max – F_min)/F_max.

Step 10 – Finite-element (FE) normalisation of levitation force  
- COMSOL Multiphysics used with H-formulation.  
- PMG field first calculated analytically and imported (Fig. 12a).  
- 3-D bulk model created (Fig. 12b); J_c set to 1.1 × 10⁴ A cm⁻² (Bean model).  
- Parametric sweep: thickness h = 2–20 mm (step 0.1 mm between 9–10 mm) with fixed 26 mm × 26 mm a–b plane; then area S varied 441–676 mm² with h = 9.5 mm.  
- Linear regression performed on F_max and F_min vs. h (9–10 mm) and vs. S (441–676 mm²); slopes and R² recorded (Figs. 13–14).  
- Experimental forces normalised to a “standard” bulk of h = 9.5 mm and S = 550 mm² using the combined thickness-and-area coefficient k_v (Table 5).  
- Engineering densities calculated:  
  – Force-area density F_s = F_min/S  
  – Force-volume density F_v = F_min/V (Table 6).

- No porosity measurement uncertainty or image-analysis threshold specified.  
- Error bars or statistical spread of force values not provided.  
- Sample identification: CPP, MPP, CM1, CM2, CM3 (CM = C-MPP).

- CAD model of the hollow-cylinder negative drawn (SolidWorks) and printed (Creality CR-5 h Pro, ABS filament, 0.4 mm wall, wax-coated).  
- Slurry cast into the ABS mould, gelled, cured 5 h at 60 °C.  
- Mould dissolved in acetone; green body dried 5 days at 50 °C, 90 % RH.  
- Organic binders burnt out at 800 °C for 24 h in air.

Step 4 – Pre-sinter & infiltration setup  
- Green preform pre-sintered 950 °C / 4 h.  
- Liquid-phase pellets (32 mm Ø × 30 mm) uniaxially pressed and stacked above, below and inside the bore of the preform; whole assembly placed on a Y2O3 base.  
- Infiltration carried out at 1060 °C for 1.5 h in air, furnace cooled. Excess liquid removed after cooling.

Step 5 – Seeded single-grain growth  
- Buffer pellets (75 wt % Y-123 + 25 wt % Y-211, pre-annealed 900 °C) capped with NdBCO thin-film seeds positioned on both ends of the infiltrated cylinder.  
- Heat treatment (air): ramp to 1050 °C in 1 h → rapid cool to 1012 °C → slow cool 0.2 °C h⁻¹ to 980 °C → furnace cool to RT.  
- Buffer pellets removed; cylinder surface lightly polished.  
- Oxygenation: 450 °C / 7 days in flowing O2.

Step 6 – Structural & microstructural characterisation  
- XRD (Cu Kα) on top surface and on ground powder; Rietveld refinement to obtain lattice parameters.  
- Optical and FESEM on polished sections (final polish 0.5 µm diamond); Image-J used to quantify RE-211 area fraction and size distribution.  
- EDAX area scan to confirm RE (Nd, Sm, Gd) incorporation.

- AC-susceptibility (real part) versus T to obtain Tc and transition width ΔTc.  
- Magnetic shielding test at 77 K: homemade copper solenoid (ID 7.5 cm, length 16 cm) producing up to 41 G dc; axial field monitored with and without the cylinder.

- Jc(B) extracted from loop width via extended Bean model:  
  Jc = 20 ΔM / [a (1 – a/3b)] with a < b the sample cross-section dimensions.  
- Flux-pinning force density Fp = Jc·B plotted versus B; normalized curves f(h) = Fp/Fp,max versus h = B/Bp constructed and compared with theoretical δκ, point- and surface-pinning functions to identify the dominant mechanism.

- Spin-coat Megaposit SPR 220-4.5 photoresist at 8000 rpm.  
- Expose pattern with Dilase 250 laser writer.  
- Develop in NaOH solution.  
- Etch unprotected YBCO in H₃PO₄ bath.  
- Strip resist in acetone.

Step 4: Resistor attachment for local heating  
- Glue a 220 Ω resistor (Loctite Stycast 2850FT) on the current pad ≈ 0.7 mm from the bridge; two Al wire-bonds connect it to the PPMS puck.  

Step 5: Electrical contacting  
- 33 µm Al wire-bonds (TPT HB05 bonder) link the sample to the PPMS puck: current leads at the two ends of the bridge, voltage taps in the middle.  

Step 6: Critical-current mapping  
- Measure I–V curves at every (T, B) point with PPMS AC transport option.  
- Define Ic with 1 µV cm⁻¹ electric-field criterion (bridge length 2 mm → 20 µV threshold).  

Step 7: MQE / quench search  
- Cool to 70 K; set magnetic field.  
- Apply a fixed transport current (expressed as %Ic).  
- Inject 0.7 s heat pulses by stepping the resistor current in 1 mA increments until a quench is detected (voltage jump ≈ 100 × noise).  
- Record the smallest resistor current that triggers a quench; compute MQE ≈ I²Rt with R = 220 Ω and t = 0.7 s.  
- Repeat for other %Ic, then change T or B; always increase absolute current as little as possible to postpone burnout.  

Step 8: NZPV extraction  
- Use voltage traces from the two farthest channels (3 and 4, 1 mm apart).  
- Measure time delay for each signal to cross a 10 mV threshold.  
- NZPV = 1 mm / Δt.

- Cs-corrected STEM (JEOL JEM-2200FS, 200 kV, HAADF) on BZO-doped piece to image nanorods (diameter ≈ 6 nm, spacing ≈ 20 nm).

- Measure Ic and n-value at 77 K, self-field, on the individual CFD and regular REBCO tapes intended for cabling (1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion).  

Step 2 – Bending-strain screening  
- Wind sample tapes (REBCO side facing former) on copper formers of decreasing diameter; record retained Ic after 45° bend.  
- Select the smallest former diameter that keeps Ic degradation ≤32 %; adopt 6.35 mm-OD copper rod + two heat-shrink layers → 6.9 mm bending diameter for cable winding.  

Step 3 – CFD tape preparation (reel-to-reel)  
- Mask 0.8 mm-wide stripes along both edges of 1 m-long SP REBCO tapes.  
- Chemically etch unmasked silver (aqueous H₂O₂:NH₄OH:H₂O 1:1:4) to create a high-resistivity degraded layer (Ri 100–320 µΩ cm²) under the future silver over-coat; remove mask; deposit silver.  
- Electroplate 10 µm Cu on 9–10 cm end sections (C1 & C3) to enable low-temperature indium soldering without Ag consumption.  
- Leave 50 cm sacrificial tail (C4) for winding grip; final usable length 30 cm.  

Step 4 – Regular tape preparation  
- Same length (1 m) and Cu-plated ends (D1 & D3) but no CFD patterning.  

Step 5 – CORC® cable winding  
- Wind two contra-helical layers (3 tapes each, 38.6° inner, 37.7° outer twist angle, 17 mm twist pitch) on the insulated 6.9 mm former; no inter-layer material added.  
- Cut sacrificial tails; obtain 30 cm active cable length.  
- Insert each cable end into a Cu tube (ID 9.4 mm, OD 12.7 mm); fill with indium solder to form 3 cm (regular) or 4 cm (CFD) termination.  

Step 6 – Room-temperature resistance check  
- Four-terminal measurement through termination voltage taps: 52 mΩ (CFD) and 44 mΩ (regular).  

Step 7 – Critical-current measurement  
- Immerse cable in liquid-N₂ (77 K) or in pumped-cryostat (65–77 K, ±0.05 K homogeneity).  
- Inject square current pulses (pulse width ≤ few 10 ms for NZPV, DC ramp for Ic).  
- Record total cable voltage; subtract terminal current-transfer component (baseline fit); apply 1 µV cm⁻¹ criterion to extract Ic and n-value.  
- Repeat for 67–77 K range on CFD cable; single-point calibration (76 K → 77 K, factor 1.15) used for regular cable.  

Step 8 – Normal-zone propagation velocity (NZPV) measurement  
- Mount 16 cm PCB equipped with spring-loaded pogo pins every 5.9 mm (one pin per outer-layer tape per twist pitch).  
- Place small NdFeB magnets under cable to create an 8 mm-long local Ic-depressed zone; trigger quench with a single current pulse.  
- Acquire pin voltages at ≥kHz sampling via multi-channel DAQ; define arrival time when local voltage reaches 0.1 V.  
- Compute NZPV = tap separation / time difference between successive taps; average left- and right-going fronts.  
- Sweep current 300–1200 A at 77 K; repeat in cryostat at 68.6, 71.3, 73.5, 77.3 K.  

Step 9 – Post-mortem inspection  
- Visually check for burn marks or degradation (regular cable failed at magnet location after 73.5 K run).

- Samples: 4 mm-wide SP REBCO tapes, 50 µm Hastelloy, 1.6 µm REBCO, 2.5 µm total Ag, no additional Cu stabiliser on cable section.  
- CFD zone: 3.2 mm width (f = 0.8), 26 cm length along each tape, Ri 100–320 µΩ cm².  
- Cable: 6 tapes, 2 layers, opposite twist, 30 cm active length, 6.9 mm final winding diameter.  
- Temperature: 65–77 K controlled by pumping on LN₂ bath; PT100 sensors at 4, 8, 12 cm heights.  
- Current: pulsed square wave (NZPV) or DC ramp (Ic); max ≈1.2 kA.  
- Electric-field criterion: 1 µV cm⁻¹ for Ic; 0.1 V for NZPV arrival time.  
- Voltage contacts: total cable taps for Ic; 5.9 mm-spaced pogo pins for NZPV.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Film growth  
- EuBCO layers (550–600 nm) deposited by PLD on IBAD-MgO buffered Hastelloy tapes.  
  – BHO-doped films: 1055 °C growth, 250 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.  
  – Undoped EuBCO: 1150 °C growth, 350 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.  
- (Y,Gd)BCO reference films grown by MOD on similar buffered tapes; BHO introduced via Hf-naphthenate precursor; 300 °C O₂ anneal 3 h.

Step 2: Microstructural characterisation  
- Cross-sectional TEM/HAADF and plan-view SEM/TEM to measure inclusion diameter (≈4.5 ± 1 nm in EuBCO; 12–14 nm in (Y,Gd)BCO), morphology (nanoparticles → nanorods with increasing BHO), separation d, grain size, twin-boundary spacing, dislocation density.  
- EDS mapping to confirm chemical identity of precipitates.

Step 3: Magnetisation measurements  
- All films cut into rectangular pieces (lateral size 3–4.5 mm) and mounted on Delrin disks.  
- Quantum Design MPMS3 SQUID magnetometer with field H ‖ c-axis.  
  – Tc determination: zero-field-cooled moment m(T) in 0.2–0.4 mT, sweep rate 0.5–4 K min⁻¹.  
  – Jc(B,T): hysteresis loops m(H) at fixed T (1.8, 20, 40, 60 K); Bean model for rectangular plates Jc = 20Δm /[w²lδ(1−w/3l)]; VSM mode used to reduce creep contribution.  
  – Magnetic relaxation (creep): after establishing critical state (ΔH = 2 T > 4H*), record m(t) every 4–10 s for 1 h at fixed (H₁,T₁); extract creep rate S = −d ln m / d ln t from linear fit to ln m vs ln t.

Step 4: Data analysis  
- Fit log Jc vs log B in the strong-pinning region to obtain exponent α.  
- Fit relaxation curves M(t) to interpolation formula M(t)=M₀[1+(μk_BT/U₀)ln(t/t₀)]^(−1/μ) with t₀ = 10⁻⁶ s to extract μ and U₀; construct μ(T,B) contour maps.  
- Compare experimental μ with theoretical values for single-vortex (1/7), small-bundle (3/2), large-bundle (7/9), half-loop (1), variable-range hopping (1/3) regimes.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Sample set: five EuBCO films (0, 1.9, 2.8, 3.8, 4.8 vol % BHO) and two (Y,Gd)BCO films (0 and 8.9 vol % BHO).  
- Film thickness: 550–600 nm (measured, Supplementary Table 1).  
- Applied magnetic field range: 0–9 T perpendicular to film plane.  
- Temperature range: 1.8–60 K for Jc(B); 1.8–60 K for creep.  
- Self-field regime identified via μ₀H_sf = μ₀γJ_sfδ/π with γ = 5.  
- Oxygen content y deduced from empirical relation 0.21y = 1.283+p (carrier concentration p from Hall data).  
- Doping consistency maintained within each growth method; absolute doping differs between PLD and MOD groups.

[Experimental Workflow]
Step 1: Target synthesis  
- A ceramic PLD target with nominal cation ratio Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:4 was prepared by a conventional solid-state reaction (details of powder calcination/sintering not given).

Step 2: Substrate selection and cleaning  
- Three single-crystal substrates were chosen: SrTiO₃ (STO), LaAlO₃ (LAO), and [LaAlO₃]₀.₃[Sr₂TaAlO₆]₀.₇ (LSAT).  
- Surface preparation procedure not specified in the paper.

Step 3: Pulsed-laser deposition of Cu-rich YBCO films  
- A 248 nm KrF excimer laser PLD system was used.  
- Laser power density: 1 J cm⁻²; target–substrate distance: 5.5 cm.  
- Two growth temperatures were explored: 780 °C and 750 °C.  
- Oxygen partial pressure during ablation: 100 mTorr.  
- Typical film thickness investigated: 40 nm (strain study) and 120 nm (microscopy study).  
- Deposition rate: ≈1.6 nm min⁻¹ (not explicitly stated whether this value applies to both temperatures).  
- After deposition the chamber was filled with 700 Torr O₂; samples were cooled at 5 °C min⁻¹ with an intermediate 1 h anneal at 400 °C.

Step 4: Reference sample growth  
- A stoichiometric YBCO target (Y:Ba:Cu = 1:2:3) was used to deposit a reference film on LSAT under identical PLD parameters (780 °C, 100 mTorr O₂, etc.).

Step 5: Structural characterisation  
- X-ray diffraction (Bruker D8 Explorer) θ–2θ scans and φ-scans on (106)/(016) reflections to verify c-axis orientation and epitaxy.  
- Cross-sectional high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (Thermo Fisher Talos F200XG2) with fast-Fourier-transform analysis to image embedded cubic domains; energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy inside TEM to obtain local Y:Ba:Cu ratios.  
- Surface morphology and compositional surface spots checked by scanning electron microscopy (NOVA NANO SEM 450) coupled with EDS.

Step 6: Electrical transport measurements  
- Temperature-dependent resistivity R(T) recorded for 40 nm films; experimental details (current, contact geometry, criterion) not specified.

Step 7: Magnetisation measurements and J_C extraction  
- Quantum Design PPMS equipped with a vibrating-sample magnetometer (VSM) module.  
- Sample size for magnetic measurements: 5 mm × 2.5 mm.  
- Zero-field-cooled M(T) taken under 20 mT out-of-plane field.  
- M–H hysteresis loops recorded at several temperatures.  
- Critical current density calculated with the extended Bean model for a rectangular plate:  
  J_C = 20 ΔM / [w (1 – w/3l)] where l = 5 mm, w = 2.5 mm, ΔM is the magnetisation width.  
- Irreversibility field B_irr determined by linear extrapolation of Kramer plot J_C^½ B^¼ versus B at each temperature (data below 35 K excluded because of large uncertainty).

Step 8: Data analysis  
- Power-law fits of B_irr(T) ∝ (1 – T/T_C)^n and J_C(T) ∝ (1 – T/T_C)^s performed to compare Cu-YBCO and reference YBCO.

[Experimental Design Details]
- Cu-excess level: 33 % (Cu/Y = 4 vs 3).  
- Substrate choice for J_C/B_irr comparison: LSAT (microwave-device oriented).  
- Thickness for electrical/magnetic comparisons: 40 nm.  
- Thickness for TEM inspection: 120 nm.  
- All comparative superconducting property data shown in the paper refer to films grown at 780 °C; 750 °C data are only used to illustrate temperature sensitivity.
